A descriptive sequence analysis of the Turkey ISKUR evaluation
Historical Turkey ISKUR Vocational Training Evaluation (2010–2013).
Study source: World Bank Turkey Vocational Training Program, public-use microdata. https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/1973

title: A randomized offer is not the same as training received

text: A randomized offer is not the same as training received
Unknown attendance and blank treatment-arm answers stay unknown. Course completion is not certification.

The official World Bank variable script confirms MIS_EC23 asks whether the evaluation-course certificate was received. We cross-checked 3,016 answered records against the derived field; mismatches: 0.
Source: World Bank related materials, including questionnaires and Create Variables File: https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/1973/related-materials

title: Only verified dates establish pre- and post-training outcomes

text: Only verified dates establish pre- and post-training outcomes

Exact admin start
and end dates
Pathway cohort: 1,546 documented attendees with all three observed outcomes
Sequence: any work → any work → formal work. The final measure is narrower.
Dates are parsed from MIS_EC7/MIS_EC8 and interview dates in the DTA. Source and outcome definitions: https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/1973

title: Four pathway groups summarize observed attendee sequences

text: Four pathway groups summarize observed attendee sequences
No follow-up work; no August formal job
No follow-up work; formal job by August 2013
Not working at baseline; working at follow-up
Clusters describe similarity, not causal program effects or fixed natural types.

Cluster assignments are average-linkage agglomerative clustering over individual Hamming distances. Counts and shares are computed from the reproducible pipeline outputs. Source: https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/1973

title: Observed trajectories differ in timing and later formal employment

text: Observed trajectories differ in timing and later formal employment
Administrative first-job milestones and earnings are summarized separately; public-use data do not include monthly job-spell dates.

Profile estimates from outputs/turkey/cluster_prevalence.csv and outputs/turkey/cluster_admin_profile.csv. Definitions are in docs/TURKEY_DATA_DICTIONARY.md. The monthly Social Security histories discussed in related research are not distributed in this public-use DTA.

title: Separation is strong; subsample stability is moderate

text: Separation is strong; subsample stability is moderate
k=5 was excluded because its smallest cluster is 2.8% (<5%). The selected k=4 solution is not a perfect pattern partition; sequences are grouped into shared outcome pathways.
Low-dimensional sequence space limits claims about latent structure.

Candidate silhouette and deterministic subsample stability values are computed from the released Turkey DTA, not externally reported study effects. The ARI compares refitted groups after nearest-medoid assignment.

title: Baseline and follow-up gaps are reported, not filled in

text: Baseline and follow-up gaps are reported, not filled in
Extreme follow-up work-rate bounds: 41.8%–46.5% among attendees with valid baseline
Descriptive comparisons only. “Not working” is not the same as unemployed; missing outcomes remain unknown.

Baseline group shares and sensitivity bounds come from the pipeline's strict dated cohort. Extreme bounds assign unknown survey outcomes to 0 or 1 for the calculation only; no imputed outcomes are stored. World Bank evaluation context: https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/954771468318313306/pdf/823060P12051400h0final0report0small.pdf

title: A valid CA result—with a clear boundary

text: A valid CA result—with a clear boundary
Observed employment pathway summaries among documented Turkish vocational-training attendees, with dated baselines, administrative follow-up measures, and explicit missingness sensitivity.
Maharashtra or Indian employment estimates; causal effects; exact month-by-month job histories absent from the public file; or outcomes for nonrespondents.
Present as a historical Turkey ISKUR evaluation (2010–2013). Keep PLFS work separate; it is cross-sectional and does not validate Maharashtra pathways.
Sources: World Bank microdata catalog (catalog 1973); evaluation report (2013); questionnaires and variable construction file.

Sources: https://microdata.worldbank.org/catalog/1973 ; https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/954771468318313306/pdf/823060P12051400h0final0report0small.pdf ; https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/1973/related-materials.
